job.title: Sales Manager, Marine Environmental Technology (China)
job.description:
Get in front of the yards, know the competition better than they know themselves, and win the business.
 
Angle Recruitment has partnered with a well regarded European maritime technology group to find a Sales Manager for China. The group's portfolio spans decarbonisation, water treatment, and environmental marine equipment, with tens of thousands of systems in service across the world fleet.
 
The role is field based and covers shipyards and owners across China, so expect plenty of time on the road. It's one of several new sales hires as the group strengthens its commercial team worldwide.
 
In short, you'll open doors and close orders.
  • Build and deliver your own business development plan for China
  • Present the group's systems at shipyards across the major building regions, for newbuilds and retrofits
  • Win orders against established domestic and international competitors
  • Keep a healthy pipeline and work closely with group sales leadership in Europe
  • Represent the business at exhibitions and industry events, including Marintec
You'll bring a track record selling marine equipment or systems into Chinese shipyards, ideally in environmental, water treatment or decarbonisation technology. You'll have strong yard relationships and be out in the field rather than behind a desk. You'll also have fluent Mandarin and good business English for working with a European head office.
 
In return, you'll get a strong product range behind you, a group investing in growth and a direct line to senior leadership. There's also a competitive package of base salary, target linked bonus and a generous monthly allowance.

job.title: Senior Technical Superintendent, Drybulk (MPP)
job.description:
Keep the bulkers in class, on budget and earning.
 
Angle Recruitment has partnered with a renowned ship owner/operator to find a Senior Technical Superintendent (Dry Bulk) for its Singapore office. The company operates a dry bulk fleet and runs its technical management with real care for the ships and the people on them.
 
The role is based in Singapore, with regular travel across the region for attendances, dry dockings and inspections.
 
In short, your job is to keep your vessels safe, compliant and trading without interruption.
  • Take full technical responsibility for a group of dry bulk vessels
  • Plan and supervise dry dockings, repairs and special surveys
  • Manage vessel budgets, spares and maintenance planning
  • Handle PSC, vetting and class matters, and close out findings promptly
  • Support and guide the senior officers on board and junior superintendents ashore
You'll bring proven experience as a Technical Superintendent and hands on dry bulk experience, whether ashore or at sea. Experience with geared bulkers, cranes and grabs will be well-regarded. You'll also have the judgement to make sound calls under pressure and the presence to hold your own with yards, class and owners alike.
 
In return, you'll join a well regarded owner/operator with a long term view of its fleet, a strong team around you and a remuneration package to match the role.

job.title: Senior Manager, Chartering & Business Development
job.description:
Angle is supporting an established ship operator to hire a Senior Chartering Manager. This person will build and lead the long-term time charter book. This role offers a path to grow into more senior leadership roles as the business develops.
  
You’ll originate and develop relationships with cargo owners and charterers, long-term time charters, this will be your predominant focus. Grow a stable cargo base that supports geared and gearless fleet. Alongside the longer-term development work, you’ll also run profitable day-to-day chartering, matching cargoes and vessels, negotiating fixtures, and taking controlled positions on third-party tonnage within approved limits.
  
This is an individual contributor role reporting to the Head of Drybulk. You’ll work closely with Operations, Finance, Risk and Post Fixture internally, and with shipowners, charterers, brokers and agents externally. Success will be measured by the pipeline of strategic accounts and long-term opportunities you build, the COAs and long-term contracts you convert, and the commercial returns you deliver. Those who perform will have the opportunity to step into broader leadership responsibilities as the platform grows.
  
What you bring
  • Significant drybulk chartering experience, ideally across more than one side of the market.
  • A proven record of winning new business, particularly COAs or long-term time charters
  • Strong market sense and an established network among cargo owners, charterers and brokers
  • The ability to negotiate confidently and build relationships at every level
  
If you’ve built long-term business before and want to do it again from a relatively small starting point, with room to grow into leadership, we’d like to hear from you.

job.title: Marine Sales Manager
job.description:
Marine Sales Manager

Angle Recruitment is currently supporting the International Marine Solution company to find a Marine Sales Manager who will lead the sales function, driving revenue growth, customer development and market expansion across the maritime sector.
This role requires a commercially focused leader who can develop and execute effective sales strategies, manage and develop the sales team, strengthen key customer relationships and identify new business opportunities. The successful candidate will work closely with Management and internal teams to ensure sustainable growth and profitability.
 
Sales Leadership & Strategy
  • Lead, manage and develop the Sales team to achieve revenue and business targets.
  • Develop and execute sales strategies aligned with the company's overall business objectives.
  • Monitor team performance and implement improvement plans where required.
  • Prepare sales forecasts, performance reports and market updates for Management.
  • Build a collaborative, accountable and high-performing sales culture.
Business Development & Customer Management
  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with key maritime customers and strategic accounts.
  • Identify and develop new business opportunities across the marine sector.
  • Understand customer requirements and provide suitable commercial and technical solutions in collaboration with internal teams.
  • Attend client meetings, maritime exhibitions, conferences and industry events to develop market presence and new opportunities.
  • Build and maintain a strong sales pipeline across existing and prospective customers.
Commercial Growth & Market Development
  • Lead commercial negotiations and support contracts through to successful closure.
  • Monitor vessel movements, fleet activities and customer developments to identify sales opportunities.
  • Analyse market trends, competitor activity and customer behaviour, providing relevant insights to Management.
  • Develop strategies to improve performance across underperforming territories, customer segments and product/service categories.
  • Ensure sales growth is commercially sustainable and aligned with profitability objectives.
Requirements
  • Diploma or Degree in Business, Marketing, Engineering or a related discipline.
  • Strong sales experience, with previous team management or leadership experience.
  • Experience within marine equipment, marine services or the wider maritime industry would be highly advantageous.
  • Strong business development, strategic planning and market analysis capabilities.
  • Proven ability to develop customer relationships and manage commercial negotiations.
  • Strong leadership and people-development skills.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and presentation abilities.
  • Proficient in MS Office and CRM systems.
  • Self-motivated, commercially minded and able to work independently.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Willingness to travel overseas when required.

job.title: Vessel Manager (Heavy-Lift & Project Cargo)
job.description:
Our client is an established shipping company with a long record in heavy lift and project cargo, moving the awkward and the oversized worldwide: wind turbine components, transformers, modules and marine equipment.
 
Technical management sits in Singapore, close to the commercial desk, so this is a role where the superintendent is part of the conversation on what the ships can lift, not just who keeps them running.
 
The role
  • You'll own a small fleet of heavy lift vessels end to end: maintenance, drydocking, budgets, crew and compliance.
  • You'll review lift plans, ballast and stability calculations and sea fastening with the cargo engineers, attend critical lifts, and keep the cranes, wires and hydraulics to class and maker standard.
  • You'll prepare vessels for charterer vetting, close out audits, manage OPEX and drydock budgets, and build a proper working relationship with your Masters and Chief Engineers.
  • Some travel, sometimes at short notice.
 
You
  • You're already a Vessel Manager or Technical Superintendent.
  • Heavy lift, project cargo or offshore construction vessels are a must.
  • You know your way around heavy lift cranes (Liebherr, NMF, Huisman or similar), ISM, class and PMS, and you're comfortable reading a lift plan.
  • Hands on, calm under pressure and commercially aware.

job.title: Head of Crewing
job.description:
One of Papua New Guinea’s largest shipowners is seeking an experienced Head of Crewing to lead crewing operations from their Lae office.

About the Company The company operates a fleet of 25+ vessels, including tugs, barges, smaller container ships, tankers and dry bulk carriers. This is a substantial, established owner (not an agency) with a significant presence in the Pacific. The role is a genuine long-term leadership position — the current incumbent is on a contractor/seafarer contract, and the company now wants a permanent Head of Crewing who will fully own the function.

The Role You will report to the General Manager (based in Port Moresby) and lead a team of six. You will be responsible for a pool of around 600 crew drawn from Papua New Guinea, Philippines, India, China, Malaysia and other nationalities.

This is an office-based role in a 24/7 operational environment. Secure transport is provided between accommodation and the workplace.

Key Requirements
  • Deep, hands-on knowledge of crewing — particularly rostering, crew planning and training
  • Proven experience leading and managing a crewing team
  • Comfortable operating in a high-tempo, 24/7 maritime environment
  • Strong organisational and stakeholder management skills
  • Previous experience with multi-national crew pools is highly advantageous
  • Willingness to work in Papua New Guinea on a well-supported basis
What's on Offer
  • Competitive base salary
  • Visa support
  • Club memberships
  • High-quality accommodation within a secure compound
  • Secure transport
This is one of the more substantial crewing leadership roles currently available in the Pacific. The company has a track record of supporting international hires and provides a secure, well-managed living environment.

To apply or discuss the role further, please reply with your CV and a brief outline of your relevant crewing leadership experience. All applications will be treated in strict confidence.

job.title: Vessel Operator, Product Tankers
job.description:
Keep the ships moving, the ports honest and the voyage result where it should be.
 
Our client is a well regarded international shipping company in the tanker space, moving chemicals and clean petroleum products across Asia Pacific, the Americas and Europe. Its Singapore office runs a mix of controlled tonnage, COAs and spot fixtures.
 
They are adding a Vessel Operator to the Pacific operations team. It's a small team that shares knowledge, reporting to the Operations Manager, with the occasional port or vessel visit.
 
In short, you will run the daily operation of an assigned fleet as efficiently and economically as possible.
 
  • Issue voyage instructions, monitor bunkers, drafts and ETAs, and maximise cargo intake at load ports
  • Nominate agents, review pro formas and DAs, and challenge any lost time in port
  • Track off hire, support demurrage and laytime claims, and check freight invoices
  • Prepare voyage estimates and keep IMOS voyage files clean, current and handed over properly
  • Oversee tank cleaning with owners and managers, and maintain vessel and port KPIs
 
You will be a well versed tanker operator, ideally from chemicals or CPP, with a sound grasp of time charter, COA and voyage charter terms. You know how ships, ports and terminals work, you understand tank cleaning and cargo handling, and you can negotiate firmly without falling out with anyone. IMOS experience is a plus. Sailing experience would also help, but it isn't required. The trade runs around the clock, so you will need to be comfortable taking a call outside office hours.
 
In return, you join a respected name with strong backing, a steady fleet and a team that invests in its people. A competitive package is on offer for the right person.

job.title: Dry Bulk Vessel Operator
job.description:
Our client, a global MNC requires a Dry Bulk Vessel Operator to oversee post-fix vessel operations of its dry bulk fleet. You will ensure safe, efficient and optimised voyage execution while coordinating closely with vessels, charterers, brokers, agents and internal teams.

Reporting to the Head of Operations, key responsibilities include:
  • Manage end-to-end dry bulk vessel operations from fixture to voyage completion for 12-13 vessels
  • Ensure alignment with Charter Party Agreement; respond promptly to events, handle laytime, demurrage/dispatch and claims
  • Oversee voyage instructions, scheduling, port calls, cargo operations, bunkering and performance
  • Coordinate with Masters, charterers, brokers, agents, terminals and suppliers
  • Monitor vessel positions, bunker consumption, speed and operational KPIs
  • Optimise voyage costs (bunkers, port expenses, agency fees)
  • Manage cargo documentation, bills of lading and letters of indemnity
  • Resolve operational issues and disputes to minimise commercial exposure
Requirements
  • Degree/professional qualification in Maritime Studies, Shipping, Logistics or related field
  • 5+ years’ dry bulk operations experience, in post-fixture, loading, unloading, demurrage
  • Exceptional knowledge of dry bulk Charter Party Agreement, laytime, demurrage and voyage economics
  • Experience with Handysize/Supramax vessels preferred

job.title: Sales Manager

job.title: Environmental Data Specialist (Shipping)
job.description:
Angle Recruitment has partnered with a well established shipping company to find an Environmental Data Specialist who can bring order to how it measures and reports its impact.
 
Like every shipowner, the business has to report its carbon emissions, waste and water use. It burns fuel at sea, uses electricity ashore, sends crew and staff around the world, and buys goods and services from hundreds of suppliers. The rules for reporting all this are clear. The data behind it is not. Some figures come from systems, some from spreadsheets, and some from a vessel emailing numbers to the office. Each office does it a little differently, so the totals are hard to trust.
 
Your job is to fix that, and make sure it stays fixed.
 
You'll sit in Finance, reporting to the Finance Controller, because the priority is numbers that stand up to an auditor. You'll work closely with a small sustainability team of four, two on the fleet side and two in corporate, who know the business and the targets.
 
In practice, you will:
 
  • Set the rules. Turn group data policy into a practical way of working, with clear owners, controls and the evidence an auditor will ask for.
  • Find the gaps. Map where every piece of carbon, waste and water data comes from, and spot the duplication, risks and manual workarounds.
  • Check the numbers. Test data from across the business, spot what doesn't add up, and explain why.
  • Deliver the tools. Build the case for practical tools and automation, then implement them within the systems that exist today.
  • Crack Scope 3. Build a sensible approach to supplier, travel and crewing data, including business travel emissions and offsetting.
  • Make it stick. Write clear guides and train the people who supply the data, so the process runs long after the two years are up.
 
You'll bring hands on experience managing Scope 1 and 2 inventories under the GHG Protocol, and a good eye for whether data is clean. You'll have designed data processes and controls that held up to review, ideally with some exposure to Scope 3 and external assurance. Shipping knowledge is useful but not essential. The client is open to someone slightly earlier in their career, as long as the carbon accounting and data quality skills are genuinely there.
 
In return, you'll get a clear brief, real influence across the business, and a competitive package. It's two years to build something that lasts.

job.title: Technical Superintendent - Australia
job.description:
Angle Recruitment is supporting a client that is looking for a Technical Superintendent to join their team in numerous locations in Australia. 
 
This role will oversee vessel maintenance, technical performance and compliance, ensuring safe, reliable and cost-effective operations.
 
Scope:
  • Oversee vessel maintenance, inspections, repairs and planned maintenance.
  • Coordinate dry-dockings, class surveys and vessel certifications.
  • Manage maintenance budgets, contractors and technical procurement.
  • Work closely with vessel crews, clients and regional teams to resolve technical issues.
  • Provide technical support across regional operations, with some travel required.
Experience:
  • Experience as a Technical Superintendent or in a similar ship management role.
  • Ideally, seagoing or shore-based experience with tugboats or offshore support vessels.
  • Knowledge of vessel maintenance, dry-docking, planned maintenance systems and class compliance.
  • Strong project management, communication and organisational skills.
  • A hands-on, commercially minded team player with a strong focus on safety and reliability.

job.title: Dry Docking Superintendent
job.description:
Angle Recruitment is supporting a client that is looking for an experienced Dry Docking Superintendent to oversee and coordinate vessel dry-docking, repair and maintenance projects.

Key Responsibilities
  • Plan, coordinate and supervise vessel dry-docking, repairs, maintenance and refurbishment projects
  • Liaise with shipyards, vessel owners, technical teams, subcontractors and suppliers.

job.title: Technical Superintendent, LNG
job.description:
Keep a fleet of LNG carriers running safely, efficiently and on budget.
 
Angle Recruitment has partnered with an established shipowner to appoint a Technical Superintendent for its LNG fleet. The role is based in Singapore, with travel to vessels, yards and vendors as the fleet requires.
 
In short, your job is to keep the ships in class, on hire and on budget.
  • Take full technical responsibility for an assigned group of LNG carriers
  • Plan and lead drydockings, repairs and major overhauls, from specification to redelivery
  • Manage vessel budgets and OPEX, and keep a firm grip on spend
  • Make sure the fleet meets class, flag, vetting and terminal requirements
  • Support the senior officers on board and be their first call when something goes wrong
You'll bring seagoing expereince on LNG carriers, with time served as Chief Engineer on LNG or as an LNG Technical Superintendent ashore. Cargo containment, boil off management and dual fuel propulsion should feel like familiar ground.
 
In return, you'll get a senior technical role in one of the most demanding sectors of shipping, the backing of a respected owner, and a competitive local contract salary.

job.title: Technical Superintendent, Bunker Fleet
job.description:
Keep Singapore's bunker tankers safe, compliant and earning.
 
Angle Recruitment has partnered with a bunker tanker operator in Singapore, the world's busiest bunkering port, to appoint a Technical Superintendent for its fleet. This is an urgent hire and the client is moving quickly.
 
In short, your job is to keep the vessels running, the inspectors satisfied and the downtime to a minimum.
  • Take technical responsibility for an assigned group of bunker tankers
  • Plan and oversee maintenance, repairs and drydockings
  • Make sure the fleet meets class, flag, MPA and vetting requirements
  • Manage vessel budgets and work with suppliers and shipyards to keep costs in check
  • Support the crews on board and respond quickly when issues arise
You'll bring tanker seagoing experience as Chief, Second or Third Engineer, holding at least a Class 1 to 3 COC, or at least 2 years as a Technical Superintendent for oil or bunker tankers. Integrity matters in this role, as does the ability to lead, work across teams and communicate clearly in written and spoken English.
 
In return, you'll get a hands on role in a busy fleet where your work is seen every day, and a competitive local salary.

job.title: Internal Risks Control
job.description:
Strengthen governance, optimise processes and drive operational excellence across maritime.

The role will focus on improving business processes, strengthening internal controls and governance, monitoring operational risks, and supporting ESG reporting across the Group.
 
Key Responsibilities

  • Support the development and standardisation of SOPs, approval workflows and internal control procedures.
  • Conduct periodic reviews across procurement, payments, claims, vendor onboarding, inventory and records management.
  • Track findings, remediation actions and improvement initiatives, providing regular updates to management.
  • Prepare reports covering observations, root causes, risks and recommended corrective actions.
  • Support the collection, verification and consolidation of ESG data and preparation of reports, disclosures and presentations.
  • Participate in cross-functional governance, risk and process improvement projects.
Requirements
  • Diploma/Degree in Accounting, Finance, Management or related discipline.
  • Experience in audit, finance, operations, compliance, risk or process improvement.
  • Good understanding of business processes, internal controls and governance.
  • CIA, CIMA or CA qualifications are advantageous.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving and stakeholder management skills.
  • Independent, meticulous and proactive with strong attention to detail.
  • Proficient in Excel, PowerPoint, MS Office and Power BI.

job.title: Head of Trade
job.description:
Angle Recruitment has partnered with an established shipping company to appoint its next Head of Trade.
 
Based in Singapore, you'll lead the trade and commercial strategy across key international markets, with responsibility for growth, profitability and execution.
  • Set and deliver the trade and commercial strategy
  • Drive pricing, yield, forecasting, capacity and P&L performance
  • Develop new commercial opportunities and strengthen existing trade performance

  • Work closely with Sales, Network, Operations, Procurement and Finance
  • Lead and develop a high-performing team

You'll be commercially driven, analytical and hands-on, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders and turn strategy into results.

job.title: Pool Manager, Tankers
job.description:
Run the pool, grow it and keep the owners in it glad they joined.
 
Angle Recruitment has partnered with an established name in the tanker market to find the next leader of its commercial pool. Several key owners already sit inside the pool, and the plan now is to take it further.
The location is flexible. There's plenty of travel, so working remotely is fine, and there are offices worldwide if you'd rather base yourself in one.
 
In short, your job is to keep the ships well employed, the owners well served and the pool growing.
 
  • Take full ownership of how the pool performs, how its service is delivered and how it grows
  • Work with the chartering team to secure the right mix of spot and COA business
  • Win new charterers and bring new tonnage into the pool, beyond the existing key accounts
  • Be the commercial face of the pool to owners, charterers and brokers
  • Keep a sharp eye on the market, competitors' positions and new trade lanes worth pursuing
 
You'll bring a tanker chartering or broking background, ideally in chemicals or CPP, and enough feel for the spot market to know how the pool wins its business. You don't need to have run a pool before, but it helps if you've played a part in one. You'll pair commercial instinct with the patience to build relationships that last beyond a single voyage.
 
In return, you'll get a high-profile role with real influence over the pool's direction, the backing of an established business, and a remuneration package to match.

job.title: Managing Director (Offshore)
job.description:
Run the business, grow it and win the contracts that keep it working.

The role is based in Dubai, with full responsibility for the Middle East, North Africa and nearby markets.
 
In short, your job is to keep the fleet on profitable contracts and the operation running well.
 
  • Set and deliver a growth strategy with ambitious commercial targets
  • Win new charters and contracts through your network in the region's energy and port sectors
  • Get the best return on the owners' assets, from fixture through to post fixture performance
  • Build, lead and keep a high performing team
  • Optimise day to day operations, compliance and the P&L
 
You'll bring senior commercial or general management experience in offshore or related sectors, and an established network with energy majors, national oil companies, contractors and port operators across the region. You'll also have a record of winning contracts and growing results, and the presence to lead a team and hold your own with shareholders.
 
In return, you'll get strong backing, a business with room to grow, real influence over where it goes next, and a remuneration package to match the role.

job.title: Marine Assurance Superintendent
job.description:
A leading offshore vessel operator is seeking a DPMA / Roaming Superintendent / Marine Assurance Superintendent to support safe, compliant operations. The fleet is primarily offshore vessels, AHTS experience would be well-regarded.
This is a hybrid role. You will work ashore and at sea, joining vessels to complete voyages, inspect operations, and turn findings into training, safety packages, DP standards and follow-up inspections.

Responsibilities
  • Plan and complete marine assurance visits across the region, including joining vessels for inspections and selected voyages.
  • Assess bridge resource management, DP operations, deck practice and crew competency in operational conditions.
  • Produce clear assessment reports and brief regional management on findings and trends.
  • Convert findings into training packages, safety campaigns, DP standards, inspection programmes and corrective actions.
  • Support DP assurance on DP-capable vessels, particularly AHTS (D-class).
  • Assist with vessel audits, OVID follow-up and close-out of actions.
  • Support incident and near-miss follow-up, including investigations where required.
  • Contribute to SMS familiarisation, Management of Change and regional safety meetings.
Requirements
  • Master Mariner (STCW II/2) or equivalent senior marine qualification.
  • Nautical Institute DP certification (Unlimited preferred) and strong DP operational experience.
  • Substantial OSV experience, ideally AHTS (D-class).
  • Sound knowledge of ISM, SOLAS, MARPOL, STCW, IMCA guidance and OVID / marine assurance practice.
  • Able to inspect a vessel, write a usable report, and turn findings into practical training and standards.
  • Willing and fit to travel frequently and complete voyages onboard across the region.
  • Clear communicator, comfortable working with multinational crews and shore management.
Working arrangement
Hybrid onshore / offshore. Significant time will be spent travelling to vessels, inspecting operations and completing voyages. Shore-based work will focus on reporting, training design, DP and marine standards, and closing out findings.
